Grandparents in our study had a high prevalence of clinically important symptoms of depression, PTSD, and grief and a high prevalence of new health problems and medication changes.

(1) the loss of a young grandchild is associated with high rates of clinical depression and PTSD; (2) grandparents who provide care for the deceased child have more severe symptoms of grief and depression; (3) Black grandparents have more severe symptoms than Hispanic grandparents and more severe symptoms than White grandparents; and (4) grandparents who provide child care experience more severe symptoms than grandparents who do not provide child care

grandparents who provide child care for the deceased young child are more likely to experience clinical depression and PTSD than non-caregiving grandparent, and Black grandparents are more likely to have severe PTSD symptoms and to think about the deceased grandchild at work.

grandparents are at risk for poor health, depression, and PTSD following the death of their young child, particularly if they provided care for the grandchild.
grandparents’ grief, depression and posttraumatic stress symptoms, and physical health are impacted when they are providing care for their deceased grandchildren.
